description: Compute capped minimum-cost maximum flow, deterministic maximum-cardinality selection, maximal induced k-core, start-relative dominator sets, and unique DAG transitive reduction. Graph observations remain tagged by directedness, vertex labels, edge multiplicity and objective.
forward: Compute capped minimum-cost maximum flow, deterministic maximum-cardinality selection, maximal induced k-core, start-relative dominator sets, and unique DAG transitive reduction. Graph observations remain tagged by directedness, vertex labels, edge multiplicity and objective.

The five implementations are std-only and have no production calls between them. Test joins can compare limit1/unit-cost admitted DAG flow with unweighted shortest-path distance; MCS/core share a simple-undirected graph after explicit validation. DAG reduction may feed reachability consumers but must not replace the graph for dominator queries. Directed-to-undirected conversion is an explicit semantic transformation, not shared representation.
inverse: Exclude flow witnesses violating capacity, conservation, exact sum of cost*flow or capped lexicographic optimum; MCS orders violating prefix priority/ties; cores omitting feasible induced subsets; dominator membership contradicted by an avoiding path; or reductions with changed closure/redundant retained edges. Exclude invalid directedness joins, wrapping checked arithmetic and treating rejected negative cycles as zero-cost empty output.

Empty and complete simple graphs both yield ascending MCS order. At k=1 a three-vertex path and triangle both yield all vertices. Adding loops to a directed chain preserves its dominator sets; adding any subset of reachable pairs to a reduced DAG preserves its reduction. Flow value/cost/witness admits changes to unused capacities/costs that preserve optimality. Thus neither the aggregate result nor these individual projections reconstructs a unique original graph.
limitations: Source/sink and all vertex IDs must retain coordinates across joins. Allocation failure is outside typed errors. Exact integer/categorical outputs admit no generic percentage relaxation; deterministic witness need not be a canonical optimum. Flow negative-cycle refusal is stronger than source-reachable refusal.
Finite tests and source-derived models are not a universal proof.
state: Flow respects capacity/conservation and exact cost; MCS chooses maximum selected-neighbor count with lowest-ID tie; k-core is maximal with live degree>=k; dominators characterize every start-to-v path, empty for unreachable v; reduction preserves reachability and keeps only essential DAG edges.
